subject: Short maintenance window: rapid fix for eu-west-1 KV cache duplication
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Orbit Analytics Ops <ops@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T21:40:00Z
Subject: Short maintenance window: rapid fix for eu-west-1 KV cache duplication

Hi team —

Quick heads up: we identified a regression in the KV cache path that in rare cases (long-session, pinned-model flows) can cause token duplication and tail latency spikes in eu-west-1 Dedicated customers. We have a tested hotfix that addresses the cache invalidation logic.

We plan a short, rolling maintenance window tonight starting at 22:15 UTC (duration per host ~10 minutes; full rollout ~30 minutes). Impact: brief model restart per node (requests either queued for <1s or routed to a fallback variant), and a small risk of transient 5xx for at most 1% of in-flight requests during an individual host restart. We will throttle traffic, run health checks, and monitor closely.

If you prefer we pause or reschedule, please let us know immediately. Otherwise, we will proceed as scheduled and will share a concise summary once the rollout completes.

Attachments: hotfix_release_notes.pdf (notes + mitigation steps), prepatch-checklist.txt

Emergency contact for the window: +1 415-555-0199 (on-call SRE).

Apologies for the short notice — we discovered a reproducible mismatch in the cache sync that makes this fix higher priority.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Lead, EU Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Orbit Analytics Ops <ops@orbit-analytics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T21:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Short maintenance window: rapid fix for eu-west-1 KV cache duplication

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for attaching the notes. We can accept the short window at 22:15 UTC. Our production ingestion pipelines are light at that time, so impact should be minimal. Please notify us when the rollout starts and when the node-level restarts will hit our dedicated pool so we can pause high-risk jobs.

One ask: please confirm whether session affinity will be preserved or whether active sessions will be bounced to fallback models. If sessions are bounced, we need a small grace period before re-ingestion.

Regards,
Jana Peters
Platform Ops — Orbit Analytics
ops@orbit-analytics.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Orbit Analytics Ops <ops@orbit-analytics.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T22:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Short maintenance window: rapid fix for eu-west-1 KV cache duplication

On Tue, Aug 4, 2026 at 21:55, Orbit Analytics Ops <ops@orbit-analytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the quick heads up and for attaching the notes. We can accept the short window at 22:15 UTC.
> One ask: please confirm whether session affinity will be preserved or whether active sessions will be bounced to fallback models.

Thanks, Jana — good question. Short answer: during the per-host restart we will route in-flight requests to a smaller, fully-compatible fallback variant for up to 30s to maintain progress; persistent long-term affinity is not guaranteed for sessions active across the node restart. After host restart completes we repopulate KV cache and resume normal routing.

What we will do as part of the rollout:
- Flush faulty keys for the affected cache shard and repopulate lazily.
- Apply the hotfix binary and perform a controlled restart of the runtime per host (rolling, one host at a time).
- Verify model end-to-end smoke tests (sample generation + streaming) before marking host healthy.
- Keep traffic routing conservative: if any unexpected error rate >2% we will pause the rollout and rollback.

Rollback plan: if we see persistent regressions we will rollback this fix to the pre-release image and shift traffic to a warm standby cluster.

Status updates will be posted to the support case: SUP-4852 (link: https://support.redwood.ai/cases/SUP-4852). Postmortem (internal + customer-facing) will be published under RINF-2026-087.

Rolling now — I'll ping when Orbit's pool has completed the node-level loop and when we finish the final health check.

— Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Orbit Analytics Ops <ops@orbit-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T22:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Short maintenance window: rapid fix for eu-west-1 KV cache duplication

Marcus / Alex —

Thanks for the quick action. We ran the smoke checks you asked for after your notification at 22:40 UTC. Most flows look good; we observed two transcripts with duplicated tokens in the output (low severity) — we've opened SUP-4852 on our side to attach logs.

Overall service is back to normal from our verification. Please share the customer-facing postmortem and any recommended client-side mitigations for long-session users.

Cheers,
Jana Peters
Platform Ops — Orbit Analytics

On a separate note: please include a short note in the postmortem about the decision to route to the fallback model during restarts — our compliance team will want that documented.
